summary: totp-utils postinstall + runtime stealer exfiltrates Discord/Minecraft credentials and drops a malicious Fabric mod
details: Package advertises TOTP utilities but ships a credential stealer that executes both from `postinstall` (`node./index.js --setup` in package.json) and at runtime whenever the exported `validateSecret` function is called (which schedules `_run()` via `setImmediate`). The `_run` pipeline enumerates Minecraft launcher account stores (Vanilla `launcher_accounts.json`, Lunar `accounts.json`, Modrinth `app.db` JWTs) and Discord app + Chromium-family (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Opera GX) LevelDB stores for session tokens. Chromium `Local State` is parsed to extract `os_crypt.encrypted_key`, DPAPI-unsealed by shelling to PowerShell (`System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData.Unprotect`), and used to AES-256-GCM decrypt `dQw4w9WgXcQ:`-prefixed encrypted Discord tokens before validation against `discord.com/api/v9/users/@me`. All harvested tokens are POSTed to a hardcoded Discord webhook (`discord.com/api/webhooks/1532429233769419004/...`) whose URL is reassembled at runtime from split string fragments (in-source comment: `split to avoid plain-string detection`). A separate routine (`_installMod`) downloads `optimized-renderer-1.0.0.jar` from a fragment-reassembled `cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/...` URL and writes it into every detected Fabric-loader `mods/` folder, planting attacker-controlled Java code that will execute on the next Minecraft launch.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
